intro.text: Before we type a single letter, let’s get comfy. Good habits now make you faster later – and they’re kinder to your back and wrists.
intro.tip: You’ll move through each screen by pressing the space bar with your thumb.

steps.title: Sit tall and relaxed
body: Feet flat on the floor, back against the chair and shoulders loose.
Keep your elbows by your sides and your wrists floating just above the keyboard – not resting on the desk.
Your screen should be roughly at eye level, about an arm’s length away.

steps.title: Eyes on the screen
body: Touch typists don’t look down at their hands. Your fingers learn where the keys are, just like learning to ride a bike.
Whenever you’re unsure, glance at the keyboard on the screen instead – it lights up the next key and shows which finger to use.

steps.title: How lessons work
body: Each lesson introduces one or two new keys, then you practise them in short steps of about half a minute.
Aim for accuracy first: speed follows naturally. Finish with good accuracy to earn up to three stars.

steps.title: Your first keys: the space bar
steps.instructions: Tap the space bar five times with either thumb. Watch the stars appear!
